_comment: Main-story betrayals of Acts I to IV (docs/STORY.md 'Main-story betrayals'): trust choices on the critical path and the betrayals that cash them in. Data: data/clans.json betrayals with 'main' and 'trust_choices'. ledger_* entries are Ledger pages (first line = title).

lines: Aldo: Juna the courier came by. She'll take your Rift report to the guild in Madderby.
Aldo: Thirty years she's carried my post. Only lost two letters. Both to Mirela, funnily enough.
Aldo: How will you write it?

a1_report_code: You copy the report into the little arrows and dots from Mirela's margins.
Aldo: Ha. Nobody has read that code in forty years. Including me, and I married it.
a1_report_plain: Aldo: Good. Trust keeps a village warm.
Aldo: So does burning letters, mind you. Never mind. Old man's joke.

lines: Vash: Warden business. When the ferry runs again, the Warden log needs the hour of the crossing.
Vash: Purely for your safety. I adore safety. It's so billable.

a1_hour_true: Vash: Dawn. Lovely. I'll write it in pencil, so it's easier to sell. To file. Easier to file.
a1_hour_false: Vash: Noon. Splendid. Noon is a very honest hour. Nobody lies at noon.
You will be on the water at dawn.
juna_struck: Juna: Your report? Delivered! To the guild. And to Mother Grell. And a copy to Haus Marrovel.
Juna: Don't look at me like that. I never charge you. I charge everyone else.
Juna: The guild sends the stamp bill, though. Postage due: 100 coins. Heavy report.
juna_caught: Juna: I sold your report to three clans. They all paid in advance.
Juna: Then they opened it. Arrows and dots. Mother Grell's clerk is still crying.
Juna: Here, your cut. A courier has a code too. Mine is 'half'.
ledger_juna_post: Juna carries every letter in the valley. She also reads them, copies them and sells the copies.
Whether the clans could read yours depended on the code you wrote it in.
hour_struck: Two Marrovel 'customs men' wait on the pier at exactly the hour you gave Vash.
Customs man: Routine search. Very routine. We do it to everyone who is you.
They pat down your lead Spirling with great care, and great interest in what it carries.
hour_caught: Down the shore, two Marrovel 'customs men' are searching an empty pier. At noon. Thoroughly.
One of them left his lunch tin on a post. Inside: a Strong Tonic and a note.
'Search the map kid at noon. Signed, V.' Vash signs his work. Pride, probably.
ledger_vash_hour: Ilo Vash asked for the hour of the ferry crossing 'for the Warden log'.
The Warden log, it turns out, is read aloud in Fenrick Kael's study.
lantern_struck: Halfway down the pier, Fenrick's brass lantern starts to tick.
A Ruskweber moth crawls out of the vent. It has been eating the wick and noting where you go.
It also ate through your purse on the way out. 80 coins gone. Thorough moth.
It flutters off towards Ashmere with your route. Somebody up there will be pleased.
lantern_caught: You know how Fenrick gives presents. Aldra told you, or his own letter did.
You drop the brass lantern into the lake. Something inside squeaks and swims off, deeply offended.
Before it sank you took Fenrick's Waking Moss out of its base. It's not his any more.
ledger_fenrick_lantern: Fenrick Kael gave you a lantern for the crossing. A Ruskweber moth lived inside and wrote down your route.
Only someone who had read Fenrick's letter, or listened to Aldra, would have looked.

lines: Sable Ruskweber leans on a crate as if she owns the quay. She probably owns the crate.
Sable: Madderby is uphill, darling. My porters carry bags for free.
Sable: The first trip is always free. It's the second trip that builds character.

a2_porter_yes: Two porters lift your satchel like a newborn. A newborn they plan to sell.
Sable: See you uphill. Your bag certainly will.
a2_porter_no: Sable: Independent. How expensive of you. My porters will be heartbroken.
Sable: They'll follow you anyway. Heartbreak needs exercise.
satchel_struck: Your satchel came back from Sable's porters lighter. Lighter by 200 coins and one map of the Woadfen.
A note inside: 'Porterage, insurance, and a small fee for the fee. With love, S.'
satchel_caught: A Ruskweber porter has followed you all week, staring at your satchel like a lost love.
He gave up at last and pinned Sable's bill to your door: 'Porterage: 0. Disappointment: priceless.'
He also left his lunch behind. A Power Brew. Finders keepers.
ledger_sable_satchel: Sable Ruskweber offered to carry your satchel up to Madderby for free.
Nothing the Ruskwebers carry arrives with the same weight it left with.

lines: Brann, Veit's helper, kneels by the rock, copying Mirela's burned words into a notebook.
Brann: It's for the guild. Honest. Veit just likes to read over my shoulder. From very far away.

a2_chalk_yes: Brann: Thanks. You're kinder than Veit. That's a low bar, but you cleared it.
a2_chalk_no: You take Brann's chalk and his notebook. He doesn't fight. He looks almost relieved.
Brann: Veit will be furious. He's always furious. This time I'll know why.
brann_struck: Ysolde: Veit Harrow was here an hour before you, with Brann's notebook. Mirela's words, copied neatly.
Ysolde: He knows she holds the Wide Rift from the inside. He left smiling. Veit never smiles.
Ysolde: He broke our lock on the way out. The guild takes the new one out of your pay. 150 coins.
brann_caught: Ysolde: Brann came by without his notebook. Veit sent him away for coming back with nothing.
Ysolde: He took the train north to find honest work in Ashmere. He said 'honest' like a rumour.
Ysolde: He left this for you. Veit's Spring Flask. Veit doesn't know yet.
ledger_brann_copy: Brann copied Mirela's burned words at the Wide Rift 'for the guild'.
Veit Harrow reads everything Brann writes. Brann has never once been allowed to keep a diary.
a2_charter: Ysolde closes the file, then opens a second one. Older. Thinner.
Ysolde: Forty years ago Haus Marrovel paid for this guild's charter. The price was Mirela's route into the Rift.
Ysolde: I sold it. She went in anyway. I've been sorry in very neat handwriting ever since.
Ysolde: Now Ottilie Kael wants your route too. She asked politely. That's the worrying part.
charter_caught: A paper bird lands on the table. Pip's round handwriting: 'Grandmother bought your clerk. Burn the copy. P.'
Ysolde burns the copy. The guild clerk, it turns out, has already left town. On a very fast cart.
charter_struck: That night the guild clerk sells a copy of your route to Ottilie Kael and leaves town.
Ysolde: He left a note. 'Sorry.' Very neat handwriting. I taught him that.
ledger_charter: Forty years ago Ysolde sold Mirela's route to Haus Marrovel for the guild's charter. This year the guild clerk sold yours.
Pip warned you only if you had kept his secret in Brindlewick.

lines: Nella, Halvard's apprentice, waves from the platform with both arms and a wax pot.
Nella: You've got the guild seal? Give it here. The hall needs a wax copy for the plate records.
Nella: Back by supper. Probably. Supper is a flexible idea in Ashmere.

a3_seal_yes: Nella: Lovely. I'll only make one copy. One is a very small number.
a3_seal_no: Nella: Suit yourself. I'll copy something else. I always copy something.
nella_struck: Sable's runners wave at you across the square. Each wears a wax copy of your guild seal on a string.
Nella: I made one copy! For the records! The records must have made the others.
With your seal on their papers, the runners drew 300 coins from the guild in your name.
nella_caught: Nella: Sable's runner offered me 300 coins for a wax copy of your seal. I had nothing to copy.
Nella: So I sold him a wax copy of my thumb. He paid. Twice. Here's your half.
ledger_nella_wax: Nella asked for your guild seal 'for the plate records'.
In Ashmere a wax copy of a seal is worth exactly what the original can draw from the guild.

lines: Halvard: Mirela's plate needs copper. A Ruskweber cart sells it at half price. Half!
Halvard: Mother Grell says it's a gift between grieving families. Shall I buy it?

a3_copper_cheap: Halvard: Half price! Grief is good for business. Someone's business, anyway.
a3_copper_honest: Halvard: The honest price. My purse weeps. My plate thanks you.
copper_struck: Mother Grell waves from the back of a Ruskweber cart.
Mother Grell: Lovely copper, wasn't it? Mined from under the Stilling. It goes quiet in a fortnight.
Mother Grell: Halvard bought a second batch on your account. 250 coins. Grief is a long business, little map.
copper_caught: Mother Grell: You paid the honest price. How dull. I had a whole speech prepared.
Mother Grell: Keep this, then. A Waking Moss, for the next person you trust. You'll need it.
ledger_grell_copper: Mother Grell sold Halvard copper for Mirela's plate at half price, as 'a gift between grieving families'.
Copper from under the Stilling goes quiet in a fortnight. So do most of Grell's gifts.
route_struck: Ottilie: Your route, dear. The guild clerk was so helpful. My people have walked it twice.
Ottilie: They even carried your bag for a while. Such manners.
Her footman hands the bag back. Your lead Spirling's keepsake is no longer in it.
route_caught: Ottilie: I bought your route from the guild clerk. Pip burned it. The child has started having opinions.
Ottilie: Never mind. Opinions are expensive. He'll grow out of them.
She leaves a basket on the step. A Spring Flask and a card: 'Get well soon. Or don't.'
ledger_ottilie_route: The route the guild clerk sold in Corvane reached Ottilie Kael. She had it walked to the silent lighthouse.
Only Pip's warning, bought with the secret you kept for him, made the copy worthless.

lines: A boy in a brass badge runs up with a sealed letter.
Boy: For Warden Kaia at the oasis! You're going that way. Everyone is. There's no other water.
Boy: Mustn't open it. It's a contract. Contracts bite.

a4_letter_sealed: You tuck the letter away unopened. It feels heavier than paper should.
a4_letter_open: You steam the seal open. A Veil water lease. Whoever delivers it signs as 'courier of record', liable for the drought.
You fold it back up, very carefully, and decide to be nobody's courier of record.
kaia_struck: Kaia meets you at the oasis gate and takes the letter with a sunny smile.
Kaia: Delivered unopened! Lovely. You're now the Veil's courier of record for the new water lease.
Kaia: That makes you liable for the drought. Only a 300-coin fine. Payable at once. To me.
kaia_caught: Kaia meets you at the oasis gate. She looks at the resealed letter, then at you.
Kaia: You opened it. Rude. Correct, but rude.
Kaia: Fine. Here's 200 coins to forget the clause. Forgetting is the best-paid job in Solenne.
ledger_kaia_witness: Kaia sent a Veil water lease through you. Whoever handed it over unopened became liable for the drought.
In Solenne nobody reads the small print. That is what the small print is for.

lines: A Veil clerk at the oasis gate rattles a ring of keys.
Clerk: The Brass Veil's pump tunnels run straight to the Sun Rift. A pass is free. Safe as a contract.
Clerk: Factor Lusk insists. He so rarely insists on anything that isn't money.

a4_tunnel_yes: Clerk: Excellent. Every step is stamped and recorded. For your safety. And for the bill.
a4_tunnel_no: Clerk: The dunes? On foot? How very free of charge. Factor Lusk won't like that.
tunnel_struck: At the end of the Veil's tunnel a clerk hands you a bill. 'Tunnel toll, lamp rent, air.' 250 coins.
Clerk: Factor Lusk thanks you for the record of your route. He'll sell it back to you later. At a discount.
tunnel_caught: Behind you the Veil's tunnel fills with sand, along with three Veil clerks who waited inside it with nets.
One of the nets blows up against your boots. Caught in it: a Power Brew. Waste not.
ledger_lusk_tunnel: Factor Lusk offered a free pass through the Veil's pump tunnels to the Sun Rift.
Free, in Brass Veil terms, means the bill comes at the other end.
juna_l_struck: Juna: Letter from Aldo! Well, I wrote it. He'd have said the same, only slower.
Juna: Also, the Veil paid me to say where you sleep. I said. While you were busy, they emptied your room.
Juna: 200 coins gone. Don't be cross. I sold you before. It gets easier for both of us.
juna_l_caught: Juna: The Veil paid me to say where you sleep. I said the lighthouse in Brindlewick. They'll love the stairs.
Juna: You kept your report from me once. I respect that. Couriers respect nothing else.
Juna: Here. Aldo's real letter. Unread. Mostly. And a Spring Flask he sent along.
ledger_juna_letter: Juna followed you to Solenne with a letter from Aldo, and sold your lodging to the Brass Veil on the way.
Whether she sent the Veil to your room or to Brindlewick depended on what she had thought of you since your first report.
